| **Summary** | No PRESENCE-specific AI/LLM clause found on its own Submission Guidelines page (https://direct.mit.edu/pvar/pages/submission-guidelines, checked live). Falls back to MIT Press press-wide policy: AI tools (ChatGPT/LLMs) cannot be listed as authors; authors who use AI to produce text/images/graphics or to collect data MUST inform editors and disclose the use transparently in the manuscript; authors remain fully responsible/liable for AI-assisted content. Policy explicitly notes individual MIT Press journals MAY have stricter/more specific rules — none found for PRESENCE at query time (2026-07-13), so this is a publisher-wide default, not a journal-verified rule. |
| **Source URL** | https://direct.mit.edu/journals/pages/publication-ethics |

### Preprint Policy

> WO2 research note (not broken down per-stage — see docs/workorders/WO2_SOFT_METADATA_BATCH.md for why): No PRESENCE-specific pre-submission preprint statement found. General MIT Press author self-archiving policy (publisher-wide, not journal-specific) permits posting to institutional repositories, personal/institutional websites, and nonprofit subject repositories such as arXiv; explicitly excludes Academia.edu and ResearchGate. This describes posting rights around publication, not confirmation that submitting a manuscript already circulating as an arXiv preprint is accepted — that specific point is unconfirmed for PRESENCE.
> Source: https://direct.mit.edu/journals/pages/authors

**Current positioning (WO2, what the journal accepts now):** Empirical quantitative VR/AR studies dominate 2026 issues: presence measurement, cybersickness, embodiment/avatars, social VR, AR/VR in education and training, virtual heritage and digital museums, health/behavior-change communication in VR. Journal also runs an active qualitative turn: current Call for Papers is a special issue "Immersed into the Metaverse: Ethnographies of Presence and Embodiment in Virtual Reality" (eds. David Berliner & Maria Erofeeva, ULB), and recent free articles include ethnographic/relational-methods pieces ("Capturing Presence as a Method? A Relational Toolkit for Immersive Ethnography in Social Virtual Reality", "Towards an Anti-ableist Ethnography of Virtual Reality").

**Methods noted as welcome (WO2, qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** Quantitative controlled experiments (presence, cybersickness, embodiment, engagement), Systematic literature reviews / survey articles, Reports on implemented systems or applications, Tutorial articles, Qualitative / ethnographic methods (actively solicited via current special-issue CFP), Forum contributions: short papers, technical notes, opinion pieces, lab reports, correspondence (looser review bar than Articles)
